analysis.title: AI's Real Bottleneck Isn't Chips Anymore, It's Capital: Goldman Warns Of Semi "Air Pocket" As Bond Market Sends The Bill
key_insights: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky (Oct 14 note) argues the limiting factor for AI may not be demand but the willingness and ability to finance and deliver supply. Financing, power, construction and equipment constraints could produce an 'air pocket' in semi supply-chain orders, possibly a 2027 or 2028 event.

ASML's Oct 14 print had strong headline numbers and a higher low end of 2026 guidance. Management told Goldman's TMT desk that 30% growth in 2027 and 30% in 2028 will not meet customer demand. The stock and Korea faded because there was no upgrade to 2027.
Goldman's TMT specialist says uncertainty about credit leading to delayed infrastructure deals is the incremental data point worrying equity investors most.

Goldman equity strategists expect hyperscalers to spend about $1.2 trillion capex next year against $1.1 trillion operating cash flow. Goldman credit strategists expect 35% of hyperscaler capex to be debt-funded, over $400 billion of issuance.

About 45% of YTD follow-on equity issuance is AI-related, within total equity issuance of about $430 billion YTD, up 98% y/y. Goldman does not expect additional equity supply to derail the bull market near term, but says rising rates would narrow the debt/equity cost gap and restrain buyback growth.

Goldman swaps MD Ilir Xholi: the USD 10y10y forward swap rate rose 47bp between Sep 22 and Oct 7 while the 2-year swap rate moved 0.0bp and 1y1y rose 6bp. The desk reads this as term premium, not a change in the expected Fed path. It cites record AI hyperscaler and chipmaker debt issuance competing with Treasuries for duration buyers in September.
The 10-day rise into Oct 7 was +41bp, larger than 99.6% of 10-day moves since 2024. 10y10y peaked at 5.38%, and on Sep 30 sat 3.5 standard deviations above its 200-day average.

Xholi's trade is to receive 10y10y, targeting 4.99% with a stop at 5.40%. Catalysts include AI-related capex funding and corporate issuance slowing into Q4, and Democratic midterm gains that could slow data center projects.

Goldman credit strategist Sara Grut: in USD investment grade, spreads are under 15% of all-in yield versus a 45% average in 2019-2021. Spreads have moved higher together with government yields since July in USD and EUR, which she calls a dual headwind, so the usual cushion is less reliable.

Privorotsky puts CCC spreads around 1,250bp, over 200bp wider since September. He attributes much of it to idiosyncratic distress in legacy media, cable and building products and is not convinced AI crowding out is the driver, but notes a few AI-vertical names with notable CDS increases. Zero Hedge cites Broadcom 5Y CDS at a record 136bp and Oracle at a record 261bp (Oct 12).

Equity tape Tuesday: S&P closed down 2bp at 7,805 on 14.776bn shares versus a YTD daily average of 18.560bn. Semis fell a 5th straight session and memory fell 4%. In Asia Hynix lost 10%+, Samsung 7.4% and Micron 3.6% after CXMT DRAM headlines. AMAT is down 15% over six sessions.
Goldman TMT basket monitor over five days: Memory Exposed -8.5%, AI Data Center -7.9%, Semis -7.6%, while the S&P is down 0.17%. Memory Exposed is still up 158% YTD.

September breadth: S&P traded 1% below its mid-August record while the median stock sat 16% below its 52-week high, the weakest breadth since the Dotcom Bubble per Goldman Prime. The real 10-year yield rose 53bp in the month, crossing the two-standard-deviation threshold historically associated with negative equity returns. CTAs made +3.8%, their best month of the year, short bonds and long energy.
SPX 3-month implied correlation is below the 2nd percentile of the past 20 years, meaning little hedging.

Warsh's Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% in September, its first hike since July 2023. Goldman economists Rindels and Mericle estimate AI price pressures add about 45bp to core PCE, about half genuine and half mismeasurement, peaking at 50bp by end-2026 and fading to 10bp by end-2027.

Goldman flow-of-funds counter-case: US L/S net leverage is 46.9% (2nd percentile on a one-year view), money market funds took in $166.37 billion in the week to Oct 7, 48% of companies' buyback windows are open by month-end, and options imply historically low daily moves. A soft CPI could squeeze positioning higher.
Zero Hedge's closing view: the debt pipeline has been shut since September, which is why credit looks calm. With $150 billion of chip debt lined up, the stress may show first in CDS screens.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman strategists do not expect additional equity supply to derail the bull market. Flow-of-funds team sees light positioning (L/S net leverage 46.9%), reopening buyback windows, money market inflows and low implied moves, so a soft CPI could squeeze people back in.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler capex of $1.2 trillion exceeds $1.1 trillion operating cash flow, 35% debt-funded with $400 billion+ of issuance. Debt supply competes with Treasuries, term premium is rising, IG spreads give little cushion, and AI-vertical CDS is widening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bull case weakens if rates keep rising and narrow the debt/equity cost gap, restraining buybacks. The 10y10y receive trade is stopped out at 5.40%.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is not the problem. ASML management says 30% growth in 2027 and 2028 will not meet customer demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Financing, power, construction and equipment constraints could cause an air pocket in orders, possibly in 2027 or 2028. Credit uncertainty is delaying infrastructure deals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit conditions easing and infrastructure deals proceeding on schedule would reduce the air pocket risk (implied by the TMT specialist's comment on delayed deals).
